---
title: "17 · Recurrent Neural Network Quantum States"
code-tools: false
toc: false
---

Any network that returns one amplitude for every spin configuration can serve as a quantum state, and this lecture builds one from a recurrent network. The chain rule of probability writes the probability of a configuration as a product of conditional probabilities, one spin at a time, and a recurrent cell carries the memory of the spins already read. The resulting amplitude is normalised by construction, and configurations are drawn exactly, one spin after another, with no Markov chain. A phase output gives complex amplitudes, and masking the conditional probabilities fixes the magnetisation, the U(1) symmetry of the XY chain. The network learns a state from measured snapshots, finds a ground state by lowering its energy, and follows the time evolution of a spin chain by fitting each time step, a least-squares problem whose damped linear system is the matrix of stochastic reconfiguration from Lecture 16.
